extracted_claims.text: The EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024, and originally set obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III to apply from 2 August 2026.

Due to delays in the availability of harmonised standards and notified bodies, the European Commission proposed (via the 'Digital Omnibus on AI'/'AI Omnibus') to extend the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations by up to 16 months.
Political agreement on the AI Omnibus was reached on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
One EU source states the AI Omnibus proposal was 'adopted' on 19 November 2025, before the stated political agreement date of 7 May 2026, creating an internally inconsistent timeline.
Following the Omnibus amendment, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.
The obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028.
One source states the extended transition for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products runs until 2 August 2027, rather than 2 August 2028.

A news blog claims that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026' the Annex III high-risk obligations date was moved again, from 2 December 2027 to 2 August 2029, citing unready standards and notified bodies.

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27 July 2026) states that the Regulation applies to operators of certain already-placed high-risk AI systems only if those systems undergo significant design changes 'as from the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', without stating a fixed calendar date in that provision.
A separate EU guidance page quoting Article 111(2) states the relevant cut-off date for already-placed high-risk systems as '2 August 2026', rather than referencing the Article 113 date.

Article 113 of the AI Act lists different application dates for different chapters: Chapters I and II generally from 2 February 2025 (with certain exceptions from 2 December 2026); Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII and Article 78 from 2 August 2025; and Chapter III Sections 1-3 (which include Annex III high-risk rules), except Article 6(5), from a later date.

The Commission's original 2024 proposal and public communications framed high-risk obligations as applying '36 months after entry into force' (i.e., around August 2027) in some summaries, alongside other statements citing 24 months for general applicability.
Several 2026-era news/compliance blog articles (pre-dating or unaware of the Omnibus) continued to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.
Annex III lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk, and is described as not an automatic list of high-risk systems but a set of use-case categories.
One source attributes the 2 December 2027 Annex III date to a specifically numbered instrument, 'Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.'

The Commission proposal reportedly tied the start of high-risk rules to a condition: rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms that needed standards and tools are available, rather than purely to a fixed calendar date.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply (high confidence). Following delays in harmonised standards and notified-body readiness, the Commission's "AI Omnibus" amendment pushed this date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence), while a separate, later deadline of **2 August 2028** applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by Annex I (high confidence). Several details — including the exact legal citation for the Omnibus, whether the new date is conditional, and scattered outdated or unverified reporting — remain unsettled.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024, with Annex III high-risk obligations originally set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [AI Act Law Art. 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Article 113 of the Act lays out a staggered structure, with Chapters I–II applying from 2 February 2025, certain provisions from 2 August 2025, and Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk rules) from a later date (low confidence) ([AI Act Law Art. 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Dates
Due to delays in harmonised standards and notified-body availability, the Commission proposed extending the Annex III application date by up to 16 months via the "Digital Omnibus on AI" (high confidence) ([Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). As a result, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), corroborated by multiple EU guidance pages ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus Enters Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, high-risk AI systems embedded in Annex I-covered products apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus Enters Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

The Commission's original proposal reportedly conditioned the start of high-risk rules not purely on a calendar date but on confirmation that necessary standards and tools are available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Scope of Annex III
Annex III lists eight use-case categories that can be classified as high-risk, rather than an automatic list of named systems (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several inconsistencies emerge across sources, many below the 0.4 confidence threshold:

- An unverified news blog claims a further postponement to **2 August 2029**, attributing it to a "final text agreed in September 2026" — this is not corroborated by any official EU source (low confidence, 0.12) ([news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)) and contradicts official guidance confirming 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).
- One source states the Annex I product-embedded deadline is 2 August 2027, not 2028 (low confidence, 0.12) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)), contradicting official EU guidance.
- The consolidated EUR-Lex text cross-references Article 113 for already-placed systems rather than citing a fixed date, while a separate EU guidance page still quotes the pre-amendment fixed date of 2 August 2026 under Article 111(2), suggesting outdated content (medium confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).
- One EU source states the Omnibus was "adopted" on 19 November 2025 — before the 7 May 2026 political agreement date — an internally inconsistent sequence (medium confidence) ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).
- Several compliance blogs, apparently unaware of the Omnibus, continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline (low confidence, 0.17) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance); [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).
- One source attributes the 2 December 2027 date to "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," a citation unverified elsewhere (low confidence, 0.14) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- The precise official legal citation for the Omnibus amendment remains unconfirmed across sources.
- It is unclear whether 2 December 2027 is final or still conditional on Commission confirmation of standards/infrastructure readiness.
- Whether all Annex III sub-obligations (registration, conformity assessment, post-market monitoring) share the same 2027 date, or whether exceptions (e.g., Article 6(5)) apply differently, is unresolved.
- Further research should track official EUR-Lex consolidated texts and Commission communications post-July 2026 to confirm the final, binding date and resolve the above discrepancies.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply (high confidence). Following delays in harmonised standards and notified-body readiness, the Commission's "AI Omnibus" amendment pushed this date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence), while a separate, later deadline of **2 August 2028** applies to high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by Annex I (high confidence). Several details — including the exact legal citation for the Omnibus, whether the new date is conditional, and scattered outdated or unverified reporting — remain unsettled.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024, with Annex III high-risk obligations originally set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [AI Act Law Art. 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Article 113 of the Act lays out a staggered structure, with Chapters I–II applying from 2 February 2025, certain provisions from 2 August 2025, and Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk rules) from a later date (low confidence) ([AI Act Law Art. 113](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Dates
Due to delays in harmonised standards and notified-body availability, the Commission proposed extending the Annex III application date by up to 16 months via the "Digital Omnibus on AI" (high confidence) ([Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and the Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). As a result, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), corroborated by multiple EU guidance pages ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus Enters Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, high-risk AI systems embedded in Annex I-covered products apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus Enters Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

The Commission's original proposal reportedly conditioned the start of high-risk rules not purely on a calendar date but on confirmation that necessary standards and tools are available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Scope of Annex III
Annex III lists eight use-case categories that can be classified as high-risk, rather than an automatic list of named systems (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several inconsistencies emerge across sources, many below the 0.4 confidence threshold:

- An unverified news blog claims a further postponement to **2 August 2029**, attributing it to a "final text agreed in September 2026" — this is not corroborated by any official EU source (low confidence, 0.12) ([news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)) and contradicts official guidance confirming 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).
- One source states the Annex I product-embedded deadline is 2 August 2027, not 2028 (low confidence, 0.12) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)), contradicting official EU guidance.
- The consolidated EUR-Lex text cross-references Article 113 for already-placed systems rather than citing a fixed date, while a separate EU guidance page still quotes the pre-amendment fixed date of 2 August 2026 under Article 111(2), suggesting outdated content (medium confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).
- One EU source states the Omnibus was "adopted" on 19 November 2025 — before the 7 May 2026 political agreement date — an internally inconsistent sequence (medium confidence) ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).
- Several compliance blogs, apparently unaware of the Omnibus, continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline (low confidence, 0.17) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance); [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).
- One source attributes the 2 December 2027 date to "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," a citation unverified elsewhere (low confidence, 0.14) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- The precise official legal citation for the Omnibus amendment remains unconfirmed across sources.
- It is unclear whether 2 December 2027 is final or still conditional on Commission confirmation of standards/infrastructure readiness.
- Whether all Annex III sub-obligations (registration, conformity assessment, post-market monitoring) share the same 2027 date, or whether exceptions (e.g., Article 6(5)) apply differently, is unresolved.
- Further research should track official EUR-Lex consolidated texts and Commission communications post-July 2026 to confirm the final, binding date and resolve the above discrepancies.
